articles.title: Rupee rises 31 paise to 94.86 against US dollar during early trade
articles.summary:
The rupee appreciated 31 paise to 94.86 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, supported by the ongoing impact of the Reserve Bank of India's structural forex interventions and liquidity-tightening measures.
Market participants attributed the rupee's continued appreciation to central bank intervention and the unwinding of long dollar positions.
However, ongoing external macroeconomic pressures are likely to temper further gains, they said.
At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.95, then gained ground to touch 94.86, registering a gain of 31 paise over its previous close.
On Wednesday, the rupee appreciated 19 paise to close at 95.17 against the US dollar.
The rupee has now crossed 95.5095.00 range, bringing 94.80 into focus, CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari said.
"A sustained break below 94.80 could open the door to another 5075 paise of appreciation. And the reduced direct dollar demand from oil companies could support the momentum," Pabari .

The Fed targets 2% inflation by a different, but related, measure.Though the initial reaction was "robust," she said -- rate futures traders quickly piled into bets on an October Fed rate hike -- investors "calmed" after parsing through the data. Higher gasoline prices drove the overall increase, and underlying inflation, while still sticky, did not take a sharp turn upward."Definitely this data point suggests that the risk to inflation remains elevated," Daly said. "The risk to inflation has gone up more, but risks are not realities, and reacting on risk when you have time to make a good decision, to me, feels imprudent."Also Read: More expensive gas, semiconductors likely pushed up inflation in US last monthDaly said that the labor market's continued stability gives the Fed room to focus on price stability.But, she said, "why force urgency when you don't need to have urgency? Why not take the time to be thoughtful and deliberate? The head of the International Monetary Fund said Wednesday that the US and other wealthy nations need to urgently tackle mounting global debt levels that are weighing heaviest on low-income countries and straining the global financial system.

"At the fund, we believe that, growth, of course, helps, but it cannot deliver fast enough the necessary adjustments," Georgieva said at the autumn meeting of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok.
"There is no magic," she said, noting some other measures would be needed. "You have to go in a direction of tightening that, bringing it down, bringing deficit down."

articles.title: Sony Vizha to launch on October 19 with Tamil Idol, Celebrity MasterChef
articles.summary: Sony Pictures Networks India will launch its Tamil general entertainment channel Sony Vizha on October 19 at 8 p.m. The channel will feature reality shows, series, films, and live cricket focusing on Tamil culture. Notable programs include Tamil Idol and Celebrity MasterChef Tamil with A. R. Rahman and Samantha Ruth Prabhu as judges. Other shows will cover themes like friendship and real-life crime cases set in Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: India needs Rs 15 lakh crore to add 91 GW nuclear capacity by 2047: CEA chief
articles.summary: India needs to invest Rs 15 lakh crore to enhance its nuclear capacity to 91 GW by 2047. The Central Electricity Authority Chairman stated that nuclear energy is a stable electricity source. Currently, India has an installed capacity of 8.8 GW, which is projected to reach 22 GW by 2031. Increased private and foreign investment in the nuclear sector is also anticipated.

articles.title: Paytm's Indian ownership rises to 56%; domestic institutions continue to raise stake
articles.summary: In a notable development, One 97 Communications Ltd., Paytm's parent company, observed a significant rise in domestic share ownership as of Q2 FY 2027. Indian investors now hold over 56% of the firm, which illustrates a positive trend towards local equity involvement. Furthermore, domestic institutional ownership has soared to 29.5%, reflecting heightened engagement from local institutional players. In contrast, foreign direct investment declined to 18.

articles.title: RBI's big rupee defence: What Governor Sanjay Malhotra told Moneycontrol
articles.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra speaks exclusively to Moneycontrol, saying the central bank is ready to do whatever it takes to ensure orderly movement in the forex market. Calling markets overly pessimistic on the rupee, the Governor underscores that financial stability remains a key input in the RBI’s policy decisions. While the central bank does not normally use monetary policy to address financial stability risks, Malhotra acknowledges that policy decisions can have a bearing on stability. Could monetary policy also be used to support the rupee? How does the RBI assess currency movements and conditions in the forex market? Moneycontrol editors decode the key takeaways from the Governor’s interview, examining how global developments influence India’s growth and inflation outlook, shape the RBI’s policy decisions and affect its assessment of the neutral rate. Read between the lines as the editors break down what the Governor is signalling and what it could mean for the rupee and the road ahead for RBI policy.
